sets.relationshipLabel: a kind of play, named — genre first, example second
sets.explanation: Tragedy and musical are genres named first, and Hamlet and Hamilton are the famous examples that follow, in that fixed order.

sets.relationshipLabel: a stage tool, then the action it exists to perform
sets.explanation: A follow spot exists to illuminate a performer, just as a trap door exists to make one vanish, tool named before its purpose.

sets.relationshipLabel: a smaller stage area nested inside the larger stage it belongs to
sets.explanation: The apron is the small forward slice of the larger stage, just as the house is the audience section nested within the larger theater.

sets.relationshipLabel: the opening moment of a span, then its closing moment
sets.explanation: An entrance opens a performance and a curtain call closes it, just as a debut opens a career and retirement closes it, on two different scales.
